title: Feature Dictionary: find definitions and units
description: Search by measurement name or concept, read the definition and units, and copy useful reference text.
objectives: Find a definition by name or concept.
Narrow the results with concept and object filters.
Read units and notes, then copy the definition.
prerequisite: Have a measurement column name ready, or start with an idea such as size or intensity. The built-in dictionary can be opened without loading a project.

scenes.narration: Open Help, then Feature Dictionary. Use this window when you want to understand a measurement column in a results table or plot.
Type size in the search field and select Area from the results. The definition appears on the right, and the matching list updates as you type.
Choose a concept and object type to narrow the definitions. Try intensity and cell. Reset the selectors to Any concept and Any object for a broader search.
Search for cell_channel_1_mean_intensity and select Mean intensity. Read the statistic and units to understand what the column describes.
Scroll down to Channel, Module and Computed by for more detail. Use the named computing function as a starting point in the API reference.

Look up cell_area and read Unit. In two-dimensional measurements it represents area; in three-dimensional measurements it represents volume. Check the measurement units recorded in your project before converting values.

Read Note for qualifications such as values already expressed in physical units. For a dictionary of the columns actually present in a database, use describe_database and export_dictionary from Python.
If no definitions match, clear the filters and try a broader term or the exact column name. Custom features may need documentation from the workflow that created them.
Select the definition text and copy it into your notes. Use the Python export functions when you need a project-specific dictionary file, then return to your table or plot.
